hypothesis: The prior complete session share of one-minute realized variance not explained by bipower variation represents a different path coordinate than the existing 20-daily-return jump ratio; if source-valid it may distinguish transient discontinuity from diffuse volatility for later SOXL-versus-SOXX action-value research. This is a hypothesis, not a proven jump or alpha factor.
method_reference: Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard, Power and Bipower Variation with Stochastic Volatility and Jumps, Journal of Financial Econometrics 2004, https://academic.oup.com/jfec/article-abstract/2/1/1/960705
formula: Within each valid SOXX raw-price session, r1=log(first raw CLOSE/first raw OPEN), later ri=log(raw CLOSE_i/raw CLOSE_i-1); RV=sum(ri^2); BV=(pi/2)*n/(n-1)*sum_{i=2..n}|ri*ri-1|; proxy=clip((RV-BV)/RV,0,1). The next native session receives the completed prior-session value only.
validity: Only complete scheduled 390- or 210-bar sessions with contiguous one-minute right edges, first09:31, terminal16:00/13:00, price_valid=1 and finite positive raw OPEN/CLOSE; invalid entire day remains unknown, no nearby-bar substitution or fill.
matched_existing_daily_family: Old soxx_jump_ratio_20 uses 20 daily SOXX returns and daily bipower; compare prior-session value, SOXX daily RV20, downside semivariance share20, prior return and momentum20 on same native sessions.
source_gate: 2018>=50 and 2019/20/21/22 each>=200 valid decision-source days; source is not a near duplicate of old daily jump ratio (absolute Spearman<0.995); 2018-2019 residual variance fraction beyond five fixed daily controls>0.05. Source gate is structural only, not predictive approval.
next_economic_gate: Only after source qualification, freeze same-anchor fee-net high-SOXL versus higher-SOXX physical action-value and matched original39/state/ordinary-minute/daily-jump/volatility controls, with day grouping and full account transmission. No current approval for a fit or SOXX claim.
